content.en: Private banks are banking companies where the majority of the equity is owned by private shareholders. In the context of the **Indian Economy**, these banks operate under the licensing and regulatory framework of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**. They are governed by the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, which ensures that they maintain specific capital adequacy ratios and adhere to priority sector lending norms, similar to their public sector counterparts.
